topic: Bidirectional Associative Containers with Const Elements in C++
explanation: In modern C++, associative containers such as std::set, std::multiset, std::map, and std::multimap are used to store sorted collections of elements or key-value pairs. When these containers are declared with 'const' elements or keys, their contents become immutable after insertion, enforcing read-only access to their stored data. Additionally, bidirectional containers like std::set and std::multiset support bidirectional iterators, allowing traversal in both forward and reverse directions. Understanding how to declare and utilize these containers with const correctness and bidirectional iteration is essential for writing safe, efficient, and expressive C++ code that leverages the Standard Template Library (STL).
